name: Chicken Florentine Meatballs
description: Ground chicken meatballs simmered in a creamy white wine sauce with sundried tomatoes and spinach.

steps.text: Preheat oven to 200°C and line a large baking sheet with parchment paper.
Shred the zucchini and squeeze out all moisture with a paper towel; discard the liquid.

Add the ground chicken, panko, egg, parmesan, garlic powder, Italian seasoning, salt, and pepper to the zucchini. Mix by hand until just combined and form into 20 golf-ball sized meatballs on the baking sheet, spaced at least 2.5cm apart.
Bake 15-18 minutes, until a meat thermometer reads 74°C.
While the meatballs bake, melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the shallot, garlic, and sundried tomatoes and cook until fragrant, 1-2 minutes.
Add the wine and cook until reduced by half, about 2 minutes. Slowly stir in the chicken broth and heavy cream.
Simmer gently for 2 minutes, then stir in the parmesan and spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Add the meatballs to the pan and spoon sauce over them. Cook 3-5 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly and the meatballs are warmed through, thinning with more broth if needed.
Garnish with extra parmesan, lemon zest, and basil. Serve over pasta.

notes: Shape meatballs a day ahead and refrigerate, or bake 1-2 days ahead and make the sauce when ready to serve. Leftovers keep 3-4 days refrigerated; freeze cooked meatballs and sauce together, or freeze unbaked meatballs, for up to 3 months.
